utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Let us have the accused brought in, please. (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can now resume. Good morning, everybody. Are the interpreters ready? Does everybody hear me? The Prosecution and the Defence? General Blaskic, do you hear?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLASKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honour, I can hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can now resume. Mr. Cayley, you will be representing the Prosecution today. Let us try to finish today -- finish with the witnesses we have today, as Mr. Harmon said we would.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, your Honours, learned counsel. The next witness is a witness who has sought protective measures from the Tribunal, in that he wishes to be known by a pseudonym and to have visual distortion of his image as transmitted to the public. If you wish, I can give a summary of what the witness will be saying and how relevant that is to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I believe since the witness is actually going to be under a pseudonym and his face will be distorted, if we could for the first part of my summary go into a private session, because the description --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: How are we going to call him?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Witness V.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could for a few moments go into a private session, Mr. President, while I give the background to the witness which will identify him to the public, who he is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, then we can go into private session. (In closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (In open session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Witness W, since that is what we are going to call you, do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: First we want you to check your identity on the piece of paper which is being shown to you, but do not say your name, just make sure that that is your name. Is that your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please remain seated and read the declaration which the Registrar is giving to you. Read it in your own language. SEJFULAH MRKALJEVIC (sworn)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness W. You have been called to testify by the Prosecutor as part of the charges that have been brought against General Blaskic, the accused, who is sitting in this courtroom. The Prosecutor has summarised succinctly and densely the essential points of your testimony. After a few preliminary questions which the Prosecutor will ask you, you will testify freely before the judges about your military investigation, further to the shelling of Zenica on 19th April 1993. Mr. Cayley, the floor is yours. Examined by MR. CAYLEY

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness W. Please relax, and remember to speak slowly because some of the language that you will be using is quite complex and it needs to be translated simultaneously into two languages. Am I right in saying that at approximately midday on 19th April a number of shells fell on the city centre of Zenica, killing and injuring a number of members of the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could the interpreter please repeat this, because I did not hear it clearly?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Obviously I need to say the question again. Am I right in saying that at approximately midday on 19th April a number of shells fell on the city centre of Zenica, killing and injuring a number of members of the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is there a technical problem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could I please have the interpreter give a complete interpretation of what you just said? Now I can hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, we are going to ask you to read your question for the third time now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Witness W, it is not your fault at all. Witness W, am I right in saying that at approximately midday on 19th April, a number of shells fell on the city centre of Zenica, killing and injuring a number of members of the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that the Chief of Staff of the 303 Brigade in Zenica carried out an investigation into the number of impact sites of these shells in order to determine the direction and distance from where the shells were fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the said gentleman did conduct an investigation about the artillery attack on the city of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that you participated in that investigation and you took part in the analysis and determination of the firing point of these shells?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the investigation, I was not present at the scene but I was with the part of the headquarters which conducted the investigation on where the shells were fired from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you subsequently attend the scene in order to confirm the findings of the individual who did the preliminary investigation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I left the brigade headquarters around 4.00 pm and went on to the scene.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all the initial findings that had been brought to the headquarters at first, were they in accordance with your findings on the scene?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown, please, Exhibit 228, which is an exhibit that has previously been entered into evidence by the Defence? This is a portion of that exhibit, during Major Baggesen's testimony, on which this witness has made certain marks. Could it be placed on the ELMO, please? Witness W, if you could explain this diagram to the judges; one or two preliminary questions. This is a portion of a city centre map of Zenica, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. This is the very centre of the city of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the court the red marks and then the black marks? I apologise, the black numbers and then the red spots with the red numbers and then the 10 and 11, the two black numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Red dots mark the positions, that is the places where the shells fell on 19th April 1993, which is positions 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and points 7, 8 and 9, which we reached later when analysing the data about the shells that fell on that date on the city of Zenica. The red line marks the direction from which the shells reached the city centre. Points 5, 7, 19, 2, 6, 24, 4, 22, 9, 23, 11 and 10 mark the deployment of units or parts of the units of the army of Bosnia in Zenica on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can interrupt you there, Witness W, these are the black marks to which you are referring, so there is no confusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said red spots marked 7, 8 and 9; in fact they are not numbered because those are shells that fell into the river, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The three shells that fell into the river are points 7, 8 and 9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness W, what is the nearest military target to any of these shell craters 1 to 6, obviously not including the last three that fell into the river.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The closest military installation to the position where the shells 1 through 6 fell is at the location marked with 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the location of the Sipad Komerc Company, which was the command post of the second battalion of the 303 Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 19th April, how many soldiers were at that station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On this location, we can say that no more than ten soldiers were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you. We will come back to that diagram at a later stage. If the witness could now be provided, please, with the photographic exhibit of yesterday, which I think is 226, and be shown photograph 6, please. I will be finishing questions in a moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Witness W, if you could explain to the court in layman's terms, so that even I can understand, how from this crater you can determine the bearing and the impact angle, the bearing from which the shell was fired and the impact; remembering, of course, the determination of the calibre of the shell from the shell remnants. We will move on to range tables and calculations in a moment. Can you first of all identify which crater this was, which number shell was this that made this mark?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This crater was caused by shell number 3 that fell in front of the Borac department store.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could now explain to the court what I just summarised to you, the determination that was made on the site?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was established at the investigation first that the calibre was 122 millimetres. The crater shows that the calibre is no greater than 122 millimetres. The position of the crater and the footprints, the traces show from what direction the shell came, and that is that the shell came -- could your Honours please follow my hand and the way I am using the pointer, this is the direction in which the shell came, (indicating) and so you can see that the lower part of the shell left a clear footprint on the road. The upper part of the shell splintered and exploded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Since I do not know if the video is capturing this, I think it is important to note for the record that the witness is pointing from the lower left-hand corner of the picture to the point of impact as indicating the direction from which the shell came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That is right. Yes, that clarification is relevant, otherwise when one rereads the transcript it might not be clear. All right, Witness W, please think for a moment about our transcript and any possible challenges or discussions that might arise from what is being said, so specify clearly by saying "from the left of the photograph", or, "starting from this point". Go ahead. Begin again, if you do not mind, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, and let me try and show you the real situation. When I was showing you with this pointer the direction of the shell, it came from this area, which means that on the ELMO, this would be on the left-hand side of the photograph. Let it be entered in the transcript like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, that is good, thank you. Is that clear, Mr. Hayman? Mr. Nobilo, it is not clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I think it would be more precise if it were said that the shell came from the left towards the right. I think that is the best precision we can make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Witness W, with your pointer indicate from where in the photograph the shell was coming to where it was going and I will put into the transcript the movement of your hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley will tell you to say things as clearly as you can in your own words and then if clarifications are necessary, Mr. Cayley will clarify for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Perhaps you can add from the lower left or the higher left or middle left.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It is difficult to get the three dimensional element. So from the bottom left-hand corner of the photograph, moving down to the centre point of the impact point. Is everybody content with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I am afraid his knuckle is in the way and I cannot see very closely.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I will move across, your Honour, and see if I can assist.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from the bottom left-hand side of the photograph, moving down indicating the arc of the shell into the centre point of the impact point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Or else put two letters, A and B if possible, that is so you add an A on the left side and B on the right side and in the transcript we can say the direction is from A to B. Let us try to move along.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: The problem with that, your Honour, is that A is somewhere up here (indicates).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Or in relation to the sidewalk, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So from the bottom left-hand part of the sidewalk going diagonally at approximately 45 degrees to the point of impact, which is the white spot in the middle of the petal-shape marks made by the shell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Does that satisfy the Defence? I think everybody has understood now. Please continue, Witness W.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of the traces left on the hard surface, the lower part of the shell fragmented and the fragments left clear traces in the form of a semicircle. The upper part of the shell exploded into space, into free space. There are no traces of it on the hard surface, but there is only the traces of gunpowder gas, which can clearly be seen on the photograph. According to this finding, and having investigated the situation on the spot, and the appearance of the surrounding buildings, and having observed the direction from which the shell came and by establishing the point of impact, to use military terminology, or rather the fixed point, which is a point for geographic orientation, your Honours, the direction of fire can be defined, and it is possible roughly to estimate the impact angle. At the same time, may I explain the calibre is determined on the basis of the appearance of the crater, or rather the depth of the crater formed by the shell. Therefore by our on site investigation, I was led to the conclusion that Mr. Hajdarevic had made a correct assessment of the situation and, taking into account everything that I observed, his conclusion was in line with mine, and that is that the calibre was 122 millimetres, that the direction of the shell was 270 degrees, according to azimut, and that the impact angle of the shell was in the range of between 40 and 44 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could now be shown Exhibit 229, please? Just to clarify a couple of points with you, Witness W, the calibre of the shell was determined from the remnants that were found at the site, is that correct, the remnants of the shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the size of the hole in the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In front of you, you have a set of range tables. Could you briefly explain to the judges the purpose of these tables and what they are used for by artillery officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Artillery officers have these tables at their disposal and they use them for determining ranges in relation to certain targets, and again in relation to the positions of the deployed artillery pieces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me, I did not get interpretation on that point. Can we just repeat what was said before that, very quickly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This table, as I was saying, is used by artillery officers in relation to the positions of the artillery and the distance between those positions and the targets, and we have data on the gunpowder filling of the artillery shells. In the case of artillery pieces of 122 millimetre calibre, the gunpowder is 3,800 grammes. That is the standard charge, standard basic charge. If an artillery officer has a desired target which is removed from the position of his artillery up to the maximum range of his artillery --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Witness W, to come straight to the point, what type of shell was used in this shelling from the analysis that was done, in the shelling of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Having investigated the situation by the team of the 303rd Brigade, it was established that a shell of normal weight was used, with additional charge and with UTF fuse. This is an impact fuse that is attached to the shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the shell explodes immediately upon contact with the ground; there is no delay in explosion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those shells are normally used when artillery is being fired against infantry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In practice, this type of shell is used in battles against the infantry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could now be shown Exhibit 230? Could you explain this diagram which you drew for me in layman's terms to the court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can. This is a diagram showing the position of the artillery, and the position at which the shell fell, the distance from the artillery weapon to the place of impact of the shell, and the following parameters were taken into account; the height of the building that provided a protection outside the town of Zenica. What I am referring to is the actual hills, the relief of the terrain, and the direction from which the shell hit the town of Zenica. Then also the difference in altitude between the place of impact and the position of the artillery weapon. I took into account also the relief of the terrain in front of the artillery weapon, its altitude, and roughly estimated the angles of the position of the barrel of the artillery weapon and the angle of impact, and I showed the trajectory, which is in military terminology called the ballistic trajectory, of the artillery shell at the moment of firing, how it moved through the air and the form of the trajectory as it hit the target.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could point to the location that you have marked in the middle, I think it is the feature Vranjaca.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the map, we see this Vranjaca relief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the highest feature over which the shell would have had to have climbed, from where it was fired from to where it was going, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is the highest feature over which the shell had to cross to reach Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the point at the extreme left of this diagram?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the extreme left of the diagram is the region of Prahulje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is where you calculated the firing point was for the weapon that fired the shells into Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the position which was calculated to find where the artillery weapon was at the moment the shell was fired on that particular date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the judges the significance of the impact angle, where the shell landed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The angle at which the shell landed tells us that the artillery weapon was about 16,000 metres away from the town of Zenica. At the same time the gunman had to take into consideration all the elements in order to overcome this natural feature, the Vranjaca point, for the artillery shell to reach the town of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the normal range of a 122 millimetre artillery piece?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The normal range, with the basic charge, is about 15,300 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how was the shell able to travel 16,000 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The shell could cover the distance and to overcome this obstacle or feature and cover a path of 16,000 metres because the artillery piece was at an altitude of 510 to 515 metres above sea level, and there is a difference in altitude as compared to the position of the shell landing, because the town of Zenica itself is at an altitude of 310 to 320 metres above sea level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So simply put, in my layman's language, Zenica is several hundred metres lower than the firing point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your opinion that the shell also had an additional charge, an additional propellant to cover the extra distance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of our findings it was assessed that the gunmen had to have used a shell with an additional charge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To conclude on this, what was the bearing of the direction of fire of the artillery piece?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The bearing was westerly in relationship to the city of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the calibre of the shell and the propellant used in that shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Calibre was 122 millimetres, with additional propellant or charge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the geographical location of the firing point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The geographical location, that is the position from which the shell was fired, is the area of Prahulje, due west of the city of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could now be shown Exhibit 231?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, I just want to understand your question. When you said what was the bearing, the bearing was westerly in relationship to the city of Zenica. What do you mean by the bearing was westerly?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: That means, your Honour, that the shell was coming from a westerly direction, it was moving -- the witness can explain this better than me. Can you explain to the judge the direction from where the shell was coming from? In fact there is a map which should explain this to you, your Honour, which is the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What is the number, 231, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: 231. If a copy of this could be placed on the ELMO? In order to confirm the firing point of this artillery, you did use other information other than the calculations that you made on the ground, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is information received from the scene, and this information was passed on to us by the soldiers who were at the front-lines, who were deployed at these fixed points, which is --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which fixed points are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In military terms these are the observation points. You usually take very dominant features of the terrain for such observation points from which a soldier could follow the situation at the front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they labelled on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they are and they are marked here as observation posts, position A, or post A; this was the observation post in the Mosor area. Point or post B, this is in the area of Studerak. Point C, which is an observation post in the area of Bila, that is more precisely Grbavica. Observation post D, which is in the area of Kuber, and the observation post E, which is in the area of Saragavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the court first of all the direction of fire and the reason why you concluded that the artillery that had fired on that day was from point 1, remembering that you are not talking to military persons.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The direction of the firing of the shell from the artillery piece in relation to the location of this particular -- at this particular map placed on the ELMO would be direction from left to right; that is from the area of Prahulje to the city of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is broadly speaking a westerly direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in relation to the city of Zenica it would be the westerly direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But on this map, it is not directly west. It is not a straight line. Why is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not a straight line because the city of Zenica is north of the equator, so the curvature of the earth has to be taken into account, and then this is a military map that is at the scale 1 to 50,000. I can also observe that it has been copied several times, so this is another generation, and this was just marked as the area of Prahulje without taking the real grid location marks, so that all this can account why it is not a straight westerly direction in relation to the city.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just for clarification, Prahulje was mentioned several times and I do not see this Prahulje on the map. Is it a map, a feature, a hill? I do not follow. Just a clarification I would like to ask.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Prahulje is a point, it is a location of a hamlet and this is what I am showing with my pointer. This is at the cross-roads of these two roads, at the intersection (indicates).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I see it now, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, that is Prahulje, which is why this area got the name, the whole area got the name Prahulje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: How far is it from Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This point, your Honour, is about 16,000 metres away from the city of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And 500 metres high?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the altitude is between 510 to 520 metres above sea level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you explain to the court why you concluded that the shelling had come from the area marked 1, which is Prahulje or Puticevo, and that the shells had not been fired from 2, 3, 4 or 5, where your information confirmed that there were HVO artillery positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the date in question, the observation post at point A relayed that around 12.15 they heard firing and observed smoke coming from the position from which the firing took place. This situation was repeated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness W, which numbered point is that on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the point marked with A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they see the smoke coming from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They observed the smoke coming from the area of Prahulje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How is Prahulje marked on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On this map, Prahulje are marked with number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The firing was repeated nine times. The information was received around 1700 hours. The observation post marked with B in the area of Studerak also reported that in the period of 1215 to 1300 hours it had heard the firing coming from the position number 1, and that the shells in relation to the position of the observation post B came from the direction of north west, going in the direction of north east. At the same time, from this same post, that is observation post B, it was reported that the HVO artillery at positions 2 and 3 at that point in time was not active.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated that the observation post at point B heard the shells going in a north-easterly direction; you mean that the shells were coming from the west?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that they were coming from the north-westerly direction in relation to the observation post, so from the north-westerly direction, north of the observation post, in the north-easterly direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This I stated in relation to the position of the observation post B. The observation post in the area of Grbavica, which is marked with C, also confirmed the information that it heard the firing from the north-westerly direction from position 1, and that the HVO artillery positions 2 and 3 during this period were inactive. In other words, the artillery was not engaged in any activity, any firing at that time. The observation post D also sent the information that they heard firing from the north-westerly direction, and that at the same time they sent the information that the positions 4 and 5 of the HVO artillery deployment were inactive. Identical information, that is similar information, was furnished by the observation post E, which is in the Saragavica area, and the observers at the observation post E provided not fully clear and unequivocal information, saying that they have heard several shells passing by north of their position which flew at a very low altitude.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you establish the positions 1 to 5 of the HVO artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The positions of deployment of the HVO artillery pieces in the Lasva River valley were established through the statements of Bosniaks who lived in those areas and who had an opportunity to observe the engineering works of the HVO positions in these areas, and that is the positions 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "the engineering works"; by that, you mean the levelling of ground in order to prepare an artillery emplacement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of these witnesses actually see the artillery pieces there, in these locations, locations 1 to 35?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several witnesses observed these artillery pieces, and a number of Bosniaks gave us information on positions marked 4 and 5 in very precise terms. This is the area of Osvidak and Bare, where they were engaged partially in setting up these positions such as bringing in lumber and making shelters for storage of the artillery shells. This information was confirmed at the time when the conflict between the forces of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO forces started, because from the positions marked with 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, starting on April 16th 1993, the HVO forces were operational.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just have a few additional questions. If the witness could now be shown Exhibit 229 again, which is the city centre of Zenica. Witness W, what was the nearest Bosnian military installation in terms of distance in metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the city centre in Zenica, that is the position marked with 1, where the artillery shell fell on 19th April 1993, the closest military position, that is the position of deployment of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was at the location marked with 11. That is the unit of the second battalion of the 303rd Mountain Brigade, which was about 250 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the margin of error with a 122 millimetres calibre artillery piece when firing from a distance of 16,000 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An experienced artillery person with this weapon at this distance can hit the target within 10 metres range.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could now be shown Exhibit 226/6 again, the photograph. Mr. President, may I move over towards the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. If the Defence would like to approach the witness as well, that is possible. I do not know if you think it is necessary, but you may if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you demonstrate to the court again the direction from which the shell was fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of the photograph and the position of the impact, this is the position of the impact (indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So approximately at a 45 degree angle from the bottom left-hand corner of the photograph. When a shell lands, does it not normally leave splash marks forward of the impact point? Why are there no splash marks in this area here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The traces would be left had the shell landed perpendicularly. That means that the marks or the splash marks would be evenly sprayed around in relation to the spot of the impact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you are saying is, had the shell landed at a perpendicular angle to the ground, it would have left a rose shape of shrapnel marks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what angle did this shell land?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Based on the traces left in the street pavement, and the gunpowder gases left, this shell could only have landed at an angle which is between 40 and 44 degrees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is why there are no splash marks actually forward of the impact point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is why there are no splash marks and this is why you have the traces of the gunpowder gases.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you. One last question and I will be finished, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: According to the summary that you made, the witness has really spoken about everything that you mentioned. Ask your final question and then we will take our break.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Witness W, you identified on I think it is Exhibit 232, the position from which the HVO artillery was fired, position 1. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was position number 1, the area of Prahulje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under whose control was that geographical area on 19th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 19th April 1993, this area was under the control of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have knowledge of the HVO command and control structure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the command structure of the HVO at that time in the area of Central Bosnia, there was the Central Bosnia operation zone area of responsibility. Its headquarters was in Vitez and it commanded over the units in the Vitez area, the area of Travnik, Novi Travnik, Bugojno, Busovaca, Kiseljak, Vares, Kakanj, Zenica, Zepce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Artillery assets within that operational group, under whose command did they fall, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Throughout the war, the artillery was always under the immediate command of the officer who is in charge of a particular area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean the officer in command of the operational group or zone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I mean the superior officer, that is the highest officer who was at that time the commander of the operational zone in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 19th April, who was the commander of the operational zone in Vitez, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 19th April, the chief officer or the commanding officer of the operational zone in Vitez was Mr. Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the artillery piece that you state fired on Zenica on that day, under whose command was that artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could only have been under his command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But he did not mention that when he said that the headquarters of Vitez commanded over Vitez, Travnik, Novi Travnik, Kiseljak. He did not mention Prahulje.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Witness W, the area of Prahulje, which area is that? Which municipality is that in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Prahulje is to the south east of Travnik, about 5 to 6,000 metres. In pre-war Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is until the outbreak of war in the former Yugoslavia, Prahulje used to be part of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, we are going to take a break, we will resume at noon. (11.35 am) (A short break) (12.05 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can resume the hearing now. Have the accused brought in, please. (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Witness W, we will now -- Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: In the break, my colleagues have told me that there is some confusion about the angle of flight of the shell, because of the use of one of the photographs. I believe we can clarify very quickly by using another photograph with the witness at the same impact point to get him to explain in layman's terms where the shell was coming from and the reason for the pattern on the ground, so if I would be given five minutes more, I believe he can explain that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You, of course, will be the one to decide, but if you want to clarify things, why not? But he did tell us from where it was coming, did he not? I do not want to get into a discussion about that with you. If you feel there are clarifications necessary, you can do it as quickly as possible. Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, on two different occasions we established the angle of the shell, first time Mr. Cayley did it from his place and the second time he approached the witness. I got up and asked for a precise description, and I think this is just repetitious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If we are going to repeat the direction, I think that the testimony of the witness was detailed enough, he gave us all the various details that we were looking for. Are you really referring only to the 45 degree impact angle?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: This is an explanation, Mr. President, of why the shape of the splash marks is as it is. What I want is to get the truth out, that is what I am after. I do not think that has happened and I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You are not the only one looking for the truth, you know. That is our first priority. I have no problem with it, but let us not leave any useful things in the shadows. But do it quickly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I will simply be showing the witness one photograph and asking him to then make a sketch plan on the ELMO to explain to your Honours exactly why the splash marks look as they do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, let us do that then.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Photograph 19, please. If I could move across to the witness, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Witness W, can you show the judges where the splash marks are on this photograph left by the fall of the shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The splash marks on this photograph are on the hard surface where the shell fell, where they fell. Then also you can see them on the remains of this vehicle, so in relation to the crater, it is on the right-hand side of the photograph, so you can see the marks on the car. Then also the glass in the shop windows, that was broken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why are there no significant splash marks to the forward or rear of the point of impact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are no significant splash marks to the forward or rear in relation to the direction of the shell because the shell came at an angle and there was no obstacle in front of it. If this car should have stood by chance in front of the position where the shell fell, then it would have been significantly damaged by fragments, or if there had been a wall, then the splash marks would have been identical on this hard surface. But because there was no obstacle, the shell fragmented and the fragments flew around into the shop window and the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you take a piece of paper and very quickly, because we do not have much time, demonstrate to the judges why there are no splash marks on the ground forward or to the rear of where the shell actually fell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the shell falls on the ground at an angle of 90 degrees. Upon impact, the fragments splinter equally in all directions and according to the splash marks, you have what we call a rose being formed. If an artillery shell lands at an angle from whatever direction, the lower part of the shell leaves clear splash marks at the target or on the ground, and it has the form of a semicircle.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you demonstrate just for this particular shell, this shell impact, exactly what happened, how the shell fell and why those marks are on the ground as they are. That is an exhibit, Mr. Hayman, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Before it gets thrown in the trash, I just wanted these diagrams to be marked as exhibits in the record, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You are right, Mr. Hayman, to say that. This might even be an essential diagram.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The shell, when it hit the ground, as I have already mentioned, the lower part of the shell created a hole and damaged the ground. The upper part of the shell, as there was no obstacle in front of it, bits flew around into the space around it, and on the ground, there are only traces of gunpowder burning, nothing else, whereas the ground in the direction of the incoming shell is seriously damaged and you see visible traces of damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So this exhibit, 232, demonstrates a shell falling at a perpendicular angle into the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at an angle of 90 degrees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this demonstrates the angle at which the shell actually fell in Zenica in this photograph, in photograph 19 of Exhibit 226?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why are there no splash marks forward of the shell on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are no splash marks in front of the shell because the shell had an impact fuse. The moment it touched the ground, it went off, it exploded so that there was only small damage at the point of impact and the shell fragments, as I have already said, from the top of the shell splintered, but they made significant damage in the road and a small crater on the lower part of the shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the forward force on this exhibit, all of the shrapnel that went forward of the shell is demonstrated on this motor car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the shrapnel which flew around, their traces can be seen on the remains of this car, on the door of this car, and the back part of the car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would understand things better if I could see the picture. What is the direction of the shell? Could you show that to us with the pointer? On the photograph, you can see there are traces in black ink. Where does the shell come from, from where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: From that direction, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So from the bottom left-hand corner of the photograph, that is Exhibit 226/19. If I give these to the Registry and then we can make copies for counsel for the Defence. Thank you to the court, thank you to the Defence for allowing me to make the clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, I suppose you have been completely illuminated about this, so I suppose you have no more questions about the impact?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am afraid nothing is clear anymore, because this is quite contrary to what the investigative judge said yesterday. Could we please now have a closed session, because I have a couple of questions which could identify the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you want a private session or a complete --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, a private session. (In closed session) [Confidentiality lifted by order of Chamber] Cross-examined by MR. NOBILO

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness W, good morning. My first question is, what is your formal education?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a highly qualified machinist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not go to the military academy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which branch of the army did you attend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I completed the school for reserve officers in Zader, in the artillery rocket units of anti-aircraft defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have no formal military education. Will you tell me please who composed the team of investigators, or was there a formal decision regarding who would carry out the investigation on behalf of the BH-Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the team was not formally composed, but the chief of staff was asked by the brigade commander to go on the spot to examine the situation, and on the basis of that examination, to make a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the chief of staff at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Major Huso Hajdarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we can now have a public debate. (In open session)

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness W, I would like to know which steps or measures, formal measures did you take in the course of that investigation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time, we went to the spot, I first found a point to determine where the shell came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make a drawing of the position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you determine with a compass where the north was for each crater?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I orientate myself so well in the town that I know exactly where the cardinal points are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With equal precision as you would with a compass?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any written document on the basis of which we could reproduce the exact impact of the artillery shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is no written document but there is a document that was compiled on the basis of the conclusions of the commander officer of the team, and on the basis of those data from the spot and from the field, the conclusions were made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But those are conclusions. I am asking about a written document which could help us to reconstruct the event, so let me ask you questions one by one. You said that there was no sketch. Did you make minutes of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make a plaster cast of the crater?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may tell you, sir, what would you do in that position? Would you have undertaken all those measures at the moment the shell landed? At the time we did not have the conditions to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you said you came in the afternoon. You could have come ten days later, it would not have been changed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I had no plaster.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore today there is no material written trace of that investigation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell me please what remains of the shell were collected, and by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The shrapnel were collected that were found alongside the wall in front of the plateau opposite the Borac department store, then the shrapnel found alongside the destroyed car in the immediate vicinity of position number 1, the shrapnel at position number 4 and the shrapnel at position number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the fuse found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It probably was, I am not aware of that, but as a team of European observers came out to investigate, if they found the fuse, they have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did not find the fuse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have in your hands on a table those shrapnel once they were collected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had the shrapnel in my hands and on the table, those that we found subsequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those shrapnel suitable for identifying the type of shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For an expert in metallurgy, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can you establish exactly the type of shell used on the basis of those shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of the shrapnel, an artillery expert can ascertain the kind of shell they belong to by the way in which it splinters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the difference in the splintering between 120 and 122 millimetre calibre shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The difference is in the size of the shrapnel, then the actual type of shell, whether it is cumulative or some other kind. Then as I have also mentioned, the shell is larger and the shrapnel are larger in the case of a higher calibre shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you about the difference between 120 and 122 millimetre calibre. There is no --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. The witness answered the question. The witness has answered the question. He said the difference between the two is the size of the shrapnel, the type of the shell, whether it is cumulative or some other kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Between 120 and 122 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness did not answer my question, because he probably misheard me. He was talking about the difference between a 152 and 122 millimetre shell. My question was 120 and 122 millimetre shell. How can he determine the difference according to the size of the shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that 120 millimetres are only for mortars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Nobilo, ask your question. It was the difference between 120 and 122 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The difference between a 120 and 122 millimetre calibre is 120 millimetre is the projectile of a mortar, and 122 millimetre is the shell of a Howitzer, of an artillery piece, so here again the differences are considerable. In the case of artillery pieces the wall of the shell is thicker, when we are talking about 122 millimetres. Also the curve of the shell differs from a mortar shell of 120 millimetres. In the case of a mortar shell of 120 millimetres, the wall thickness is smaller, it was produced using a different method and the shrapnel are even smaller than those in the case of 122 millimetre shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, please, the shrapnel that you collected, what was the size of those shrapnel? How did it vary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The size varied from a large walnut to a diameter of 5 to 6 centimetres, about the length of a finger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of those shrapnel, you said that you could determine the calibre.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible to determine on the basis of those shrapnel whether there was an additional charge or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not possible to determine what kind of charge was used on the basis of the size of the shrapnel. The type of charge is defined on the basis of the distance between the artillery piece and the target.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you well? You found the place of impact and then you determined where the artillery piece would be and then you said in order to cover that distance, there must have been additional charge, so you did not establish it on the basis of material traces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That cannot be established by those traces. It is determined by the casing. The basic charge is 3,800 grammes and this means that the gunpowder charge is 186 grammes, and there are four different degrees, first, second, third and fourth and this depends on the target aimed for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Talking about additional charge, if there had not been any additional charge, from what maximum distance could Zenica be hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From a distance of 14,000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the maximum distance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With 122 millimetre calibre shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave us the parameters for the Howitzer 122 millimetres, and I think this is just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is a quote from a book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, you did not give us full information on what the artillery person is using when using a Howitzer. What portion of the maximum distance is used operationally? What is the usual standard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me give you the procedure, so that their Honours could understand it well. First the position that is targeted is set out, and when the artillery piece is first placed in the position, then the geographic orientation is set out. Then the markers are used, these are sticks two metres long and they are about 30 millimetres thick, and they are marked with red and white stripes. Then the phosphorescent markings can be placed on them. These sticks are then placed in front of the artillery piece, depending on the distance of the desired target. Let us say the artillery piece is where I am right now. I would first determine the fixed position of this artillery piece, its position in geographic terms in the area. That is, I would determine the direction of the north and together with my team, who all man this artillery piece, I would mark the directions in which I was going to operate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We understand that, but that was not my question. What maximum distance does the artillery personnel use for operational purposes? Is it not true, in other words, that two-thirds of the maximum distance is the operational distance that it is used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it when used defensively?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two-thirds for the defence purposes and one-third for the enemy positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The additional propellant is used in which cases?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depends on the personnel and it depends on the purposes, let us say two-thirds up to one-half of the third third.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what would that be in terms of percentage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be about 85 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, what would be the maximum range without the additional propellant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The maximum range of the 122 Howitzer would be 15,300.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier on, you said 14,000?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that was not the question that you had posed to me originally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what would be the 85 per cent of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 85 per cent of this, in this situation, given where the artillery piece would be, would be from 15,500 to 16,000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you one more time: what would be the maximum range of the 122 millimetre Howitzer with the standard propellant charge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be 15,300 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then how can we -- how do we get to the number 15,500 to 16,000?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It is going very fast for the interpreters and for the judges as well. I would like us to refocus the discussion. What is the influence of the additional charge, and the theoretical maximum range? Does one need -- for your demonstration, do you need an additional charge? That is what it seems to me. In any case, let us try to go a little more slowly for the interpreters' sake and also for the judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well, I will try. Witness W, what we are trying to clear up is first of all the standard range of the 122 millimetre Howitzer standard --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this question has already been posed three times, the standard range.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Perhaps it was asked, I am speaking for myself, not for my colleagues, but personally I did not understand it very well, even though the question was asked. I have no objection myself to its being asked again, so that the judges who are here before you will understand themselves. It is also a request for the interpreters, so it is a simple question: what is the maximum range. Let us try to make these questions very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Indeed it is important. What is the standard operational range of the 122 millimetre Howitzer of the standard charge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is 15,300 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this a maximum or the operative?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the maximum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you about the operative. You told me that up to 85 per cent is used as the standard range.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 85 per cent of the maximum range is used when the artillery piece is used in defence and that is more than two-thirds, in order to achieve the desired effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 15,300 is the maximum range, except for a defence protective position where you reduce it by 15 per cent, winding up with 85 per cent of the range. Have I understood correctly, Witness W?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. When I am in a defensive position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If the judge understood it, then I think everyone will understand it. Continue, Mr. Nobilo. What is your next question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move forward, even though things are a bit contradictory. In order to achieve the maximum range, what conditions have to be fulfilled in order for a shell to reach the maximum range?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All conditions in terms of climate have to be achieved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What temperature would that be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 15 centigrade, then the wind velocity does not have to be great. Optically it has to be clear, and also the artillery piece needs to be at a higher altitude than the target, so that the range can be achieved where the shell falls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about humidity and the rest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what I also tried to mention, the atmospheric conditions have to be met.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on the traces in the asphalt, in the pavement, could you determine the calibre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the basis of the traces in the asphalt, I could determine the calibre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you achieve that, through observation or measurements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Simply by observing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you a similar question that my colleague asked of you earlier. We are not artillery persons, our source is Major Baggesen and we talk about this rose or this splash mark. According to him, it is the forward traces that it makes, and now you are saying that it is backward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like a question to be asked, first. The question has not been asked, or at least I did not hear the end of the question. You said that according to the Major, the traces were in front. What is your question, Mr. Nobilo. Does he agree, does he not agree? Do you agree, do you not agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I asked the witness whether on the basis of what I asked him, does he still insist that the splash marks are made backward rather than forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That is a question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When an artillery shell falls to its target, the splash marks are made backwards if the shell hit at an angle. The rest of the shrapnel wipe out everything forward if there is no obstacle in front of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that in photo number 6, and this is Exhibit 226 -- could we please have the usher show the witness Exhibit 226, the photographs from Zenica? I would like photograph number 5 shown. You said that in the photograph number 6 that it was taken in front of the department store Beogradanka.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not what I said. This is number 3 impact in front of department store Borac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Does this photograph correspond to photograph number 5? Is it the same shell? Please can we have the usher show the witness photograph number 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to make a point that Mr. Nobilo made absolutely clear about what Major Baggesen said. He did not state what Mr. Nobilo stated. I have the transcript in front of me here. His exact words were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, just a moment, let us get some order here. Right now this is a cross-examination. If you want to contest something you can do it when you exercise your right of reply, otherwise you are going to fall into a Romantic German legal system and it is going to be a confrontation between both of you, but I do not think that is really what you are looking for. Let Mr. Nobilo do his demonstration and after that, you can ask any further questions you like. Do you agree to that -- you seem to agree, although you seem to be resigned. All right, but, of course, you have the right to your reply and the right to be resigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is your court, I will do as I am told. I am just concerned when previous witnesses' testimony is misrepresented to the court, that is my only concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, think about what you want to ask while this demonstration is being done. Mr. Nobilo, what photograph are you trying to show -- about which one do you want to show that there is a contradiction? Go ahead, but please be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I do not want any contradictions. I want to ask a simple question, whether the photographs number 5 and number 6 represent the same point of impact of the same shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Photograph number 5 was taken from the direction of the department store Beogradanka, and the arrow points to the point of impact of shell number 1 from which 16 people were killed and 30 injured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, you asked a question. We want to know whether this is the same impact on photographs 5 and 6. That was the question, was it not, whether it was the same impact. That is your question, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Would you please answer, is it from a different angle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is not the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, now go back to your question using one photograph, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, yes. You said that the shells impacted at an angle of about 40 to 45.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On average.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, on average. So at a distance of about 100 metres from the shell, what height is it from the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You would have to calculate it mathematically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you done that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not strictly speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the point of impact was, the angle was at 40 to 44 degrees. How did you determine that, approximately or by some exact method?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In those moments, we only had some standard equipment, anglometer and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you use that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Anglometer is determined first by the azimut. Then you observe the point of impact itself, the shape of the impact, and you compare the cavities, that is you determine the centre point of this cavity and then you calculate the angle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am interested when you position your anglometer at the surface; how did you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You clear it up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would be the deviation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five to eight per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both plus and minus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly what I mean, in both directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When determining the direction after 16 kilometres, how much deviation can you calculate there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About one degree, so that would mean about 300 metres. This would be just my own estimate without any measuring.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where are the fragments now, the shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is probably kept for this type of situation, because it was mostly collected by the European Monitors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What the military commission had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was, I believe, turned over, because at that time they were the only type of body who did this kind of investigation at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you do not have these fragments any more in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who analysed the shrapnel in the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Who was examining them and who said that it was calibre 122?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Huso Hajdarevic, specifically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did see them, I would have had to have been an expert in metals or an expert in artillery to have made a full analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You showed us a map, and I would like that Exhibit 231 be shown to the witness, if the usher would please do that. By showing with your pointer, could you show us where the Serbian artillery was positioned on Mount Vlasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In relation to position number 1, and please follow the direction of my pointer, the Serbian artillery was in this direction, which is north-westerly of this position (indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you position your pointer between the Serbian artillery and Zenica, so we can see where they would have been, the angle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many degrees is in this angle between Vlasic and position number 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to me, it is 50 to 55 degrees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the exact positions of the Serbian artillery on Mount Vlasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, the exact positions of the Serbian artillery on Mount Vlasic was on the Vlasic plateau, but they could not have reached the city of Zenica with 122 calibre Howitzers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about a bigger calibre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With a bigger calibre, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before this event, did the Serbs guarantee the safety of Zenica -- shell Zenica? How about after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what positions did they later shell from the Vlasic plateau area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the area of Kukotnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, I am not objecting to the question, but we are missing a portion of an answer, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, there are a lot of missing parts in a lot of the questions. I have noted it. I know that Mr. Nobilo dropped some of his questions, perhaps he decided he would give them up as he went along. But you have a good ear, it is true, there is a missing part of this question, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I do not think it is Mr. Nobilo's fault, I think the interpreters did not pick it up because it is going so quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Maybe I can make the observation that the Serbs were shelling with the calibre 130 millimetres, and that did not come into the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: That was never asked, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think a lot of things are getting confused here. I am glad that you said that. Ask your questions, ask them again if you want, but do not go that way. Do not just affirm things without questions and answers being provided. We are kind of lost in ballistics here. Perhaps this is the impact of the break which is looming before us. Perhaps it would be best for us to stop. In any case, we are not going to finish this morning with Witness W, who also needs to rest. Sharpen your equipment and we can start again at 2.45. (1.00 pm) (Adjourned until 2.45 pm) 19 20 21 22 23 24 25 (2.45 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can resume the hearing. Have the accused brought in, please. (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Witness W, did you have a chance to rest up a bit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can now resume. Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The question of 130 millimetre shells and 122 millimetre shells; can the difference between these two calibre shells be noticed, judging by the shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, by the traces of the shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the difference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The difference is that the crater of 130 millimetre gun is larger and the splash marks are larger and longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But can you judge by the shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, also by the parts of the shell, that is by the shrapnel, one can define which weapon was used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the difference between 120 shrapnel and 130 shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The manufacture is different. I already mentioned earlier on that a metallurgical expert can easily distinguish between the two, because the quality of manufacture between 130 millimetre and 122 millimetre shell differs; the way in which the shrapnel break also differs, depending on what size shell is used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to us laymen, what do you mean difference in quality of the shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you see, 130 millimetre weapon, so-called boat cannon, is a far-reaching weapon and it is used for destruction purposes. It is fired in order to incapacitate facilities. Upon explosion, the shell breaks up into larger parts, larger shrapnel, the crater is larger and the traces are more visible is compared to the 122 millimetre calibre gun.
