On the other hand, the 122 millimetre shells, their shrapnel are smaller, the wall of the shell is thinner and the splash marks are smaller in relation to those left by a 130 millimetre shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much thinner is the wall of the shell and how much smaller in the average are the shrapnel of 122 shells as compared to 130 millimetre shell; could you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not be able to give you the exact answer to that question, but it is visible. It can easily be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could I ask the assistance of the usher to show the witness a map? It is a customary, normal map from the former JNA of the area of Travnik, and I would like to ask you to tell us whether next to number 73, where it says "Oraske Stijene", are those the slopes of Mount Vlasic? If I may, Mr. President, I should like to approach the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go ahead. If Mr. Cayley also would like to approach, please do? As you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to show us on the map on the ELMO where the beginning of Mount Vlasic is, where it begins?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mount Vlasic begins from the region of Mala Peca, because the inclination is considerable and there is a considerable difference in altitude here, because Travnik is at an altitude of some 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please show us the area of Mount Vlasic that is visible on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On this map we can only see the slopes above Oraske Stijene, number 3093 on the chart, Oraske Stijene. These are the beginning, the first slopes of the plateau. Above there there are Paklarske Stijene, which is further up Mount Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: (Not interpreted). Could the usher please bring us exhibit number 29.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I would like to point out this is a protected witness and we cannot use the camera to focus on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What is the problem?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We would have to have a completely closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The features of the witness must be hidden, so while we are showing the map, let us have a completely closed session. (In closed session) [Confidentiality lifted by order of Chamber]

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We are at a closed session now, so we are free to move. Would you please draw on this foil the direction of the shell's movement as far as Puticevo. I will give you a blue marker to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Defence counsel use a microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you please draw on this foil the direction from Paklarevo to Zenica, the spot where the shells landed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Paklarevo to the centre of Zenica. I do not see why you want me to do it from Paklarevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that was the position of fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said Oraske Stijene, Paklarske Stijene and then the plateau.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From Prahulje to Zenica, will you please draw the line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marks map).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the transcript, the blue line indicates the direction of artillery fire from Prahulje to Zenica, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now will you please draw an assumed possible direction of movement of the shell from Vlasic, from the direction of Vlasic to this same point in Zenica, which we will mark in red.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have liked to have had a map with the grid references, but one has to know where on the Vlasic plateau the artillery of the army of Republika Srpska was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But I assume you can manage as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if the witness does not know where the artillery was on the Vlasic feature, should he be putting a line in to represent where it was coming from? Because the Vlasic feature is a mountain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nobilo. What you are having the witness do has to be very specific. You have to tell him what your intention is. I suppose you want to show that there were Serb batteries in those mountains and it has to be put into the transcript that you are asking Witness W that at the point from which the projectile left, you find significant, because that is why you are asking the questions. Otherwise, it is absolutely incomprehensible. All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, could Mr. Nobilo ask the witness first whether he knew where the artillery was on the Vlasic feature. If he does, he can draw the line in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness started working on it, but I can repeat my question. The witness said that on the Vlasic plateau, the Serb artillery was positioned. My question now is, could he draw in the line between the direction where that artillery was positioned and Zenica, or rather the spot where the shelling took place. This plateau on Mount Vlasic is not on the map, but the witness is a soldier, he is a professional military man from the region, he knows very well where the plateau is and I assume he can assume where the plateau is, so I think he could indicate a possible line of fire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could draw in theoretically this direction of fire, but if you have a proper map with a Vlasic plateau, then I could indicate from the region of Kukotnica towards Zenica, because then it is possible to indicate the line of fire for your orientation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It is a bit touchy to have the witness do things on a map which he does not really have in front of him, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do not need the exact position from where fire was fired, I just need a direction of fire, and as soon as that line enters the map, he can draw in the line. I only need the direction, not the actual position, the spot from where it came, so I do not need to have the actual spot from where the gun was fired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. The witness will point out this direction but in his right to reply, Mr. Cayley will bring in clarifications, either through questions he is going to ask or other things the witness is going to say through this demonstration and then, of course, this is how we are going to proceed. Do what you can, Witness W, in trying to indicate the orientation from which the shell was fired, but subject to the reservation that you do not have an exact map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, do you really need the direction or the distance between Vlasic plateau and Zenica. Is not the distance the main preoccupation?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No, my main concern is the direction, not the distance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marks map).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness W. I would like to say that for the transcript that the witness at the Defence's request drew this line, but that there were reservations about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the transcript it would be necessary to indicate that the possible direction coming from Vlasic is indicated in red and the possible direction of fire from the HVO position is indicated in blue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, you have made this clear. Can we be finished with our closed session now, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, Registrar. (In open session)

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I should now like to ask for Prosecutor's Exhibit 91, please. Could it be placed on the ELMO? Could the usher please take the pointer -- all right. Would you please look at this picture and tell us from what direction did the shell come in this photograph, and will you put your pointer in that direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The shell came in relation to this picture from the direction of the bottom right-hand corner, as the picture faces me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me now, how do you determine that this pointer which indicates the direction of the shell is not five centimetres up or down? How can you calculate that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could be 20 centimetres up or down, I am not on the spot to be able to measure the traces, the splash marks, to clean the actual spot and to determine the central point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But to what extent would you say that this pointer could be moved up or down and yet to correspond to the traces on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That depends on the situation on the spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you determine on this photograph the direction from which the shell came in view of the splash marks left on the asphalt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You know when using photographs that one can only make rough estimates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, in your opinion, there is no precise method whereby the direction from which the shell came in view of the splash marks on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a precise method?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is a precise method, which has to be done on the spot, given all the optimal circumstances and all the necessary resources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us, please, what are those conditions and what are the optimal resources that one needs to have to be able to determine with precision the direction from which the shell came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To determine the exact direction of the shell, or rather to define the impact angle of the shell, the place has to be cleaned, the splash marks copied using plastic or plaster. Then one has to indicate the furthest point to which the shell left a mark, and then take a photograph of that position from all four cardinal points and from several angles, to photograph at the same time the position of the facilities around the place where the shell fell and finally make an estimate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore this is a highly specialised approach to dealing with this problem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, if all the necessary conditions are in place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we have all those conditions, and once we have done all that, how do we do the calculation? Is there a rule in terms of the range of the fan and things like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Artillery men, people who are experts, define this on the basis of the investigation, after all these steps have been taken, and comparing their findings with the range tables for that particular artillery weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The impact angle appears to be important from the standpoint of distance, but what about the direction, left or right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is also important for the direction, because on the basis of this fan-like splash marks made by the shell, the impact angle also affects the direction, because upon impact, the shell leaves this fan-like splash mark left and right of the point of impact, and to the rear, there are very clear and obvious traces, with a crater, and in the direction of the incoming shell, or rather to the front of the point of impact, those marks are less pronounced and few in number. To the front of the shell, in most cases there are traces of gunpowder gases following the explosion, and this can be seen from this photograph which was partly in colour, where you can see these gunpowder traces to the left of the photograph from halfway up to the top of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you have not answered my question whether there are any rules regarding the spread of gunpowder gases and then, on the basis of those rules, can one determine the direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, for an artillery shell, if you have the data and the parameters, before that up to a million test shells are fired, so when you know this, then it is easier to answer how one can establish with certainty what kind of shell was used, what direction it came from, at what angle and distance and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you well, that every shell does not leave identical splash marks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is why I said that up to a million test shots are fired to get the proper exact parameters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of this photograph, can you determine the direction from which the shell came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of this photograph, as I have already said, you cannot insist that I tell you whether it is 5 centimetres up or down, but this is direction from which the shell came.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can the technical department take a shot of this as a photograph? I think we could use it later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Would you speak a little more slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. You have just told us that in view of the fact that this is a photograph, the assessment is five centimetres plus or minus, which means a total of ten. You told us that deviation of one degree in the angle of the impact angle implies 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, you have turned my statement upside down. Your question was, if there is a deviation of one degree in relation to the defined line of fire, how does this affect the result, so you are misinterpreting me. I said that if an estimate is made according to which the azimut or the angle is 271 degrees, then the artillery weapon means had to be moved by 300 to 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that was my interpretation. Does that mean if it is moved by ten degrees, that is ten times more, by 3,000 or 5,000 metres, what would that mean at a distance of 26 kilometres? If 130 millimetre calibre shell is used, how will this effect the result?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The effect is much greater.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how much greater?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you offhand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This drawing that you must made, the blue and red lines, what is the difference in degrees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In relation to the position of the shell and the firing positions in Prahulje and Kukotnica, those are azimuts. You cannot compare the azimuths, where for Prahulje it is 270 degrees and Kukotnica, where the difference is 310 to 320 degrees, which is a difference of 45 to 50 degrees in the azimut, if you know what that means. Please, let me explain myself. I am not trying to convince anyone of anything, I just want to make myself understood. If the north here according to my view is camera number 3 that means in the azimut, 270 degrees would be the edge of this blue chair, so that is the 40 degree angle. The difference between the azimut, the 270 degrees -- if a weapon is in Prahulje and a weapon in Kukotnica, then the difference is increased by the difference in altitude. Prahulje is 510 metres and Kukotnica is 1,510 metres altitude; plus Kukotnica has a feature of 1,940 metres in front of it, so there are considerable differences. You are trying to lead me on to say that the fire came from Vlasic. All the data that we have and my statement on the basis of that data shows that the fire came from the azimut of 270 degrees and that an artillery weapon of 122 calibre, millimetre calibre was used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we have no translation from Bosnian into Croatian, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to me it is azimut.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is that the same as "angle"? I am afraid we do not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that we get to where we are going in this. You have your thesis, Mr. Nobilo, the witness has his. We cannot spend the whole afternoon on this issue, although I am not disregarding the importance of that. I would like us as judges to arrive at certain conclusions. We are the ones who must be convinced. I have two questions. Is it probable that the shell came from the Serbian batteries, and second, what is your feeling about that? These are the two questions. Is it possible and is it probable? You have your ideas, but I would like you to answer very simply; is it possible or probable? We do not want to spend the entire afternoon talking about photographs. Mr. Nobilo, I think the witness has explained his method, you have your thesis and the witness has his. Is there a possibility, technically speaking, that the shell came from Serbian batteries that would be a certain number of kilometres from the HVO batteries to which you have ascribed the origin of the shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am sorry that in my testimony and through the questions of the gentleman we have confused you. May I explain? At that point in time, units of the Serb Army had batteries on the Vlasic plateau, and that was 130 millimetre calibre gun, which has a range up to 32,000 metres, which means that it could reach the town of Zenica. Its firing position, which has been defined, satisfies all artillery conditions according to deployment and position. At the same time, let me add at that time this 130 millimetre cannon did not operate, did not attack Zenica. 105 millimetre, 122 millimetre and a Howitzer of 152 millimetre calibre were used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You are answering the facts, the events, saying what happened, conclusions you drew from that, but this is not quite the technical answer. In other words, if I have understood what you are saying, it could have been a shell from those batteries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that we can move to another question now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What is the rule? Are artillery weapons positioned on a hill or at the foot of a hill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depends on the situation and the commander in chief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the rule?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The rule is a rule, but I am telling you, it depends on the situation and the commander in chief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When asked by his Honour Judge Riad, you said that the difference in altitude, that the altitude was between 510 to 520 metres between the Zenica and the place from where it was fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not the case. You confused it. My answer was that the city of Zenica was at the altitude of 310 to 320 metres above the sea level. The positions of the artillery pieces, that is the 122 millimetre Howitzer at Prahulje was between 510 and 520 metres above the sea level, so the difference between the position of the artillery piece and its target was about 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When presiding Judge Jorda asked you a little while ago, you said that Zenica was hit by 122 millimetre and 105 millimetre. Was that on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was talking in general and this is how I responded to the presiding judge as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You drew the trajectory between the artillery piece in Prahulje and the target in Zenica. How did you come to that calculation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is what the artillery specialist should do. I just drew it in a lay method, so this is the trajectory that a shell would take based on the initial velocity, and it would follow this trajectory for about two-thirds of the way, then it loses its speed, so after having been fired, the shell -- after it was fired from the artillery piece, it follows the trajectory for about two-thirds, so it is not the full one-half and it is not full two-thirds, so you could characterise it maybe as two- or three-fifths of the trajectory with full acceleration. After about that, the trajectory becomes a descending ballistic trajectory, so it would not be a fall but it would be a gradual curve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But for the ballistic curve, how did you calculate that? What is the formula?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I already mentioned, there are the artillery experts. They take all the relevant parameters and then calculate it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that is not what you did.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I did was draw what was asked of me by hand and I can do it again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is not exact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not the exact mathematical calculation. From there you can just glean how and what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On this map, you showed us the observation posts A through E. Whose observation posts were these, let us say observation post A. That is exhibit number 231. Could you please put it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These observation posts belong to the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. After the conflict of 16th April 1993, the HVO forces at first were pushed away from the city of Zenica towards the Lasva River valley, and also from Bila and Guca Gora, so all these observation posts belonged to the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, who were in the immediate vicinity of the front-line between the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you define, determine these units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think there is a need for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But could you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Due to the national security reasons, I would not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But this is information from 1993 and this is a trial where a person's life is at stake. Mr. President, would you please decide, since we are talking about events of 1993 and the witness refuses to divulge the name of the units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: First of all, I think this is part of the examination-in-chief. The witness is protected, I am not sure that this is the most significant thing for you, even if you are the one who judges your own strategy. The Tribunal has its opinion as well. Therefore it is not necessary to go any further in this type of question. Have you any other questions you would like to ask, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, I do, thank you. The reports on what artillery pieces were operating at the time, was that a written or an oral report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a written report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see these reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does not matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I would just note for the record, your Honour, these reports that have been related are obviously hearsay statements. We are trying to identify the source and the identity of the declarants. We obviously cannot cross-examine this man about it and if he refuses to answer, then we have absolutely no way to identify the source of the information and seek our right of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you want us to go back into closed session, Mr. Hayman, Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: A solution to this, Mr. President, may be that we can take a break, I can speak to the witness, find out what his concerns are and maybe bring a solution so the Defence can get a reasonable answer to the questions they are asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. We will take a ten minute break. Will that be enough for you, Mr. Cayley? Is ten minutes enough? We will take a fifteen minute break then. (3.35 pm) (A short break) (3.50 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will now resume the hearing. Have General Blaskic brought in, please. (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, I hope that we had a positive break. Rather a French expression to say a positive break, but nonetheless I hope you had a positive break.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We did, Mr. President. I think there was a dual concern the witness had and I think it should be put on the record to make it absolutely clear. We all have to understand that 1993 was a difficult time, there was a conflict going on in that area, that these are still sensitive matters for the Bosnian government. The other concern I think by the witness was that his identity would be apparent to the public if he was to discuss these matters. He is prepared specifically to answer two questions, and that is firstly the units of the Bosnian army which were present in those observation posts and he is prepared also to clarify for Defence counsel the exact nature of the reports that were made in respect of the HVO artillery in that area, but his responses would be limited in that manner and I would ask the court to limit any cross-examination for the reasons that I have just stated. And also a closed session, in order that his identity is not released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Private session and two specific questions, Mr. Nobilo. Not a private session, a closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There will not be any type of projection, so we do not have to have a completely closed session, since we are not projecting anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I would just like to know whether there will be anything projected or if we are just going to be showing maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: These are verbal answers. There should be no public transmission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Right then, a private session but no transmission to the public. What about the transcript, is the transcript under seal as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It should be under seal, your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Only for these two questions. Mr. Nobilo, the Prosecution has stated the two questions that you can ask. (In closed session) [Confidentiality lifted by order of Chamber]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The Defence is satisfied. However, we just wanted to expand it in one aspect. Has the witness seen these reports at all, or has he heard of anyone regarding these reports? This is the area that we are also interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I think the witness can answer that question, yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Witness W, you agree to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Right then, there will be three questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. So in accordance to what the member of the Prosecution said, I will ask three questions. To which units these observation posts belong, A through D.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Observation post A was 306th Mountain Brigade. Number 2, 314th Mountain Brigade. Observation post C was the consolidated forces of the 325th Brigade, that is not the complete regiment. Post D and post E belong to 303rd Famous or Celebrated Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is letter B, I think, is it not? I think it was letter B.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, instead of number 2, it should be put B, so the record should be corrected. So the record was not clear on one point. The second battalion of the 314th Mountain Brigade covered which observation post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Observation post B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Observation post B, very well. The written reports that were compiled, did you see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see the written reports, but through the exchange of data and information with the superior command, these reports were also made available to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn about what you have talked to us today about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the commanding officer of the III Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not like to answer that question, he is an operations officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this officer receive these reports directly from the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, directly from the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think you have finished, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We understand we are limited and we will move on, but I cannot say we agree or stipulate to have our ability to learn the source of the information with a higher degree of precision, but we will proceed if that is the court's direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, this is the court's direction. We have to respect the agreements reached between the parties. Mr. Nobilo, do you have any other questions you would like to ask as part of your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, very briefly, one or two additional questions and I will be finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can go back to public session now, I believe?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let us do so. (In open session)

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In general, people from whom you received your information as to where certain artillery pieces were located, were these local villagers, did they have expert enough knowledge so they could distinguish the guns and Howitzers and particular calibre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, the situation is Bosnia-Herzegovina was such that every child knew what a Howitzer was, what a gun was, what an anti-aircraft gun was, what the hand grenade was, et cetera, so the situation was such that everybody had to know each weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including calibre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up to a point. The expert people did know this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I correct in stating that there are different kinds of firing position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the operation zone in Bosnia, were there different operational groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I right, and you can correct me if I am wrong, that the Howitzer 122 millimetre belongs to the class of brigade artillery pieces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depends on the operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So according to the tactics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it can belong to the brigade, it depends on the types of combat operations that are being executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, this concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have but a few questions to ask the witness. I anticipate in the region of five to ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But you are not going to go back into teaching us a course on military ballistics, because the court has received a great deal of information on this subject and I think the witness must be a bit tired. Go ahead, supplement or correct certain points of the cross-examination. Re-examined by MR. CAYLEY

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Witness, is it normal to use an additional propellant or charge in a shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is very usual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the optimal range of a 122 millimetre artillery piece with an additional propellant in the shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I already mentioned that to the gentleman, with additional charge or propellant which is the fourth degree, the optimal range is nearly 18,000, or more precisely 17,800 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a final clarification on this point; what is the distance between the HVO artillery piece at Puticevo and the impact points in the centre of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The distance from the position of the artillery piece in Prahulje to the point of impact in the centre of the city of Zenica is about 16,000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry, Prahulje is a more accurate reference point on the map, but that is in the Puticevo area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated that the best evidence for doing this type of examination is to be on the spot as you were at the time and actually see the crater physically; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Photographs can only really demonstrate the techniques which you used at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the photographs demonstrate the technique and also show the history of what occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were cross-examined at some length on the difference in the positions of the artillery, the HVO artillery at Prahulje and the Serb artillery on the Vlasic feature. You stated to the President when he asked you a question that it was possible for Serb artillery to hit Zenica; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember and again, I repeat, the artillery of the army of Republika Srpska also had a possibility to shell the city of Zenica, but with the artillery pieces of 130 millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The shells that hit Zenica on 19th April 1993, is there any possibility that those particular shells were fired from the Vlasic feature in your mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there is no doubt that these artillery shells were fired from Prahulje and I cannot see a way for them to have been fired from Mount Vlasic, given on the trajectories and the splash marks as shown on these photographs. I am really sorry that I did not have a chance to explain to the gentleman here how this actually looks in reality.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you. We are just going to show one photograph again, Mr. President, to try and establish which impact point -- this is the photograph that the Defence produced a moment ago. If the witness could be shown that exhibit? I am not sure which number it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The original photograph was 91, your Honour. The reproduction with the chopstick is D83.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hayman. So this has become a new exhibit of the Defence then? Your question, Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any idea which impact point this was of the nine shells that fell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have an idea and I believe that I could ascertain which one it was, even though I did not see the surroundings. With your permission. The spiral line here is a decorative piece of metal that is used on the body of the Yugo 45 vehicle. From this crater in the direction of the upper right corner, the distance is about 2.5 to 3 metres. This is the photograph of the first artillery shell that fell on the city of Zenica, and which killed 16 persons and seriously injured around 30 persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, can you refer that particular photograph to any of the larger photographs that you have seen, which show the whole area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that it can be defined.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is the last point. If you could look through those photographs and identify a photograph that was taken from a further distance of that crater.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It cannot be defined based on photograph number 4, photograph number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can I have the interpretation again? Can it be defined?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it can, based on photograph number 4, photograph number 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me, the judges do not have the photo album either. Is there at least one for the three judges?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We can place it on the ELMO, Mr. President, you should be able to see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, all right, I withdraw my comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Photograph number 5, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On photograph number 5, the crater is shown and the marks are shown by the arrow where the artillery shell impacted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the forward blast of the shell? Is there any object there which demonstrates the forward blast of the shell, on that photograph that you have on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On this photograph, I have no other objects except for the passenger vehicle, which is the Yugo 45 model, which in relation to that point of impact is turned in the direction of north east, and has been destroyed as a result of the impact of the shell. I refer here to the spiral shape of this ornamental metal strip belonging to this vehicle. The shape and outlook of the crater which was photographed from the direction of north west.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Could we see where the north west direction is on this photograph, please? The car is north east, if I have understood that correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, the car is facing north east, so you see where it is facing. So it is facing towards the centre of the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you indicate from where the shell came from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, that is the question. Thank you, Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From this location (indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are indicating that the shell came from over the top of those buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the shell arrived from behind these buildings, that is between the first and the second building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It landed where the arrow is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it landed where the arrow is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this vehicle, the Yugo 45, took part of the force of the forward impact of the shell; in fact was probably thrown sideways, I would think?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If there is a way to enlarge this photograph, the car was parked -- in this photograph where I defined the direction for the gentleman of the Defence, the vehicle was parked at the very top left corner, parked, but the explosion turned it so that following the explosion it turned to face in this direction, that is in the direction of north east, looking from the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just place the small photograph back on the ELMO? We have almost finished. Where did you say the vehicle was parked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The car was parked in the upper left corner of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that not the upper right corner as you look at the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From my -- I am looking towards the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. As you look at the photograph, it is the upper right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The top right corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Riad?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness W, when did you arrive on the spot of the explosion exactly? Was it the same day of the explosions, was it afterwards? When was that exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was on the same day, about 4.00 pm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you think that the outlook and the shape of the crater was still intact completely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can assure you that it remained the same until late into the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your conclusion, your very firm conclusion was that it could be the result of 122 calibre and not 130 calibre, with the result that it could not have been from the Serbian side? I am sorry for my question as a layman, but I want just a clear view. You affirm that according to your eye's witness, let us say, when you arrived, you mentioned that it could be the result of 122 calibre and was easy to be shot or to be directed from Prahulje, since the optimal range would be 17,800 and the distance was only 16,000, whereas if it came from the Serb side, it should have been 130, which did not result in the same impact. Is that right? Did I gather rightly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, you have understood quite clearly that 130 millimetre weapon creates a larger crater and larger splash marks which are visible. Its lethal effect is greater than a weapon of 122 millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was no trace of that, no trace of 130 millimetre calibre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were no such traces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just another layman question. Is there a possibility to know, judging by the impact on the ground, what kind of weapon, I mean if it was a Serb weapon or a Croat weapon, could you know from the impact on the ground that the weapon was Serb or Croat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of the impact itself, without knowing the other data, it would be difficult to make an estimate, because both the HVO and the forces of Republika Srpska had identical weapons. But by comparing the data, it is clearly possible to come to the conclusion that the army of Republika Srpska could only have fired from positions on Mount Vlasic using artillery weapons, that is 130 millimetre gun, because all other artillery pieces would not have had the optimal range to reach the town of Zenica, because the Vlasic plateau at that moment was the closest point of the positions of the forces of Republika Srpska, closest to the town of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Shahabuddeen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Witness W, correct me in case I misunderstand your testimony. I understood you to be saying that these shells were 122 millimetre shells, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that on that day, it was not possible for 122 millimetre shells to reach Zenica from the Serb positions on Mount Vlasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not possible, because the distance is considerable between the Vlasic plateau and Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would your answer hold good even if the Serbs were to use an extra charge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because the distance between Zenica and the Vlasic plateau is about 28,000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would exceed the range of shells of this kind, even if they were used with an extra charge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The end limit, the extreme limit for 122 millimetres is 18,000. Anything beyond that, there is no point firing at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do bear with me. As you have heard from counsel, we are all laymen in the court. We have to do our best to appreciate and assess your evidence, being the evidence of one who is more acquainted with these matters than we are. Do answer me this question: can different weapons discharge 122 millimetre shells, different types of weapons I mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they cannot, sir. Your Honour, when one mentions calibre, then we are thinking of the internal diameter of the barrel, and the technical characteristics every weapon has, including the definitions of its abilities. Thus a 122 millimetre weapon has its properties defined, and the same applies for all other types of artillery weapons. Projectiles are not of the same diameter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the range of the shell would not be dependent on the type of weapon used to fire it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the difference, the range of a weapon depends on the type of weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me follow this through, and do again bear with me. The only claim I have to intervene in this field is my encyclopaedic ignorance of it. Could it be that 122 millimetre shell, if discharged by one type of weapon, might have a range which is different from the range which would be had if the same shell was discharged by a different weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may, let me try and explain. It will take a little time, so I beg your indulgence. Your Honours, this is, of course, in simplified form to make it more easily comprehensible. Every artillery weapon has its own calibre and the calibre is the diameter of the barrel, through which the projectile is fired. Therefore no other calibre can fit. For example, if you have 122 calibre, you cannot use 152 calibre shell. In such a case, the persons manning the weapon would get killed and the weapon itself would be destroyed. There are also differences regarding the discharge chamber, the firing chamber, because a 122 millimetre Howitzer uses a shell. 152 Howitzer gun uses separately the shell and the gunpowder filling. They are not together -- charge. An M46 also uses separately the shell and the charge, that is the difference. So let me further explain with an example. 152 millimetre projectile cannot be put into a 122 Howitzer or 133 millimetre cannon, because their diameters of the barrels and of the shells differ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, I thank you for the lesson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do not particularly wish that drawing to be made an exhibit, but if it is the wish of the parties that can be done. Very well. Could you answer me this other question? You spoke of an extra charge being used to launch these projectiles. Did you see any physical feature on the ground which indicated to you that an extra charge must have been used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have already explained. An additional charge is used to achieve a desired effect. It can be seen and ordered only by the superior officer in command of the firing positions where the weapons are positioned and the crew manning those positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do well to remind me of that, but actually my question was directed to a different point. Was there anything on the ground which indicated to you that an extra charge was used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were no traces on the ground, but by comparing all the data regarding the capacity of such an artillery weapon, and its positions from where it fired against the town of Zenica, they led us to conclude that an additional charge was used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me explain that I am trying very hard to follow your reasoning processes, the process of reasoning which led you to the conclusion that an extra charge was used. It was not based on any finding of any physical feature on the ground. As I understand you, and you correct me, your reasoning process was this: that on analysis of the physical features relating to the point of impact, you concluded that the line of fire was directed to Prahulje, and then you reasoned backwards to say, "well, it could have come from Prahulje if an extra charge was used", and therefore as you concluded that it did come from Prahulje, your final conclusion was that an extra charge was used; was that the process?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Upon arriving on the spot I defined it, the splash marks and the traces and determined the calibre. By comparing the subsequent data that we obtained through exchange, it was confirmed what kind of weapon was used and the assumption as to where it came from, and defining the distance from the point of impact to the position of the artillery weapon led me personally to conclude that an additional charge had to be used and was used, additional to the regular charge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. One last question, you arrived on the scene I think at 4.00?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, about 4.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when the shells actually landed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the shells were falling, I was in the brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you within hearing distance of the falling shells?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear the shells coming in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I heard them falling, when they fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only when they impacted and exploded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: A final question, Witness W, after this very long and tiring testimony, but as my colleague said, you have given us quite a course on ballistics and now we know ballistics better. In your opinion, all of these fires, could they have been directed at military targets? Could it have been the result of an error, that is the fact that there were so many civilian victims? Were there military strategic military targets that might have been the target in fact of that firing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it is in my personal interest to destroy a strategic military target, I would certainly not target it when there is the greatest frequency of people in the square in the centre of the city. That is my first point. Secondly, my artillery weapon would be directed towards its target, and thirdly, the HVO knew very well where the military strategic targets in the city of Zenica were situated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore in your opinion there were no shell impacts near the military facilities, for example the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, because the closest military facility was about 250 metres away. That was the closest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A final question. I noted that you spoke about fragmentation. The shell that was used, was that a fragmentation shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may? Let me try and explain to make things clearer. In the first place I must apologise to the ladies, I hope they will not misinterpret my drawing. An artillery shell is cast, it is cylindrical in shape, it is rounded in front and there is a fuse attached to it. Inside, there is cast trotil and the purpose of that is upon impact the time fuse, it is one of the possible types of fuses for artillery shells, ignites and detonates the explosive within the shell, and at that moment, the shell fragments. Its fragmentation is evenly distributed to all sides, if it impacts under right angles in relation to the target. However, if the impact is under a different angle other than a right angle, then the fragmentation is again the same, but the splash marks are different. So as to not to confuse you, this is a standard artillery shell charged with trotil. There are also so-called "cassette" artillery shells.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe that Judge Riad has another question he wishes to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Witness W, you just mentioned to the President that the shells fell in the centre of town something like 250 metres away from any military installation, and that the place of these military installations were well known by the HVO. My question is, what is the margin of error in launching any shell by a military expert, and not by a layman like here? What is the margin of error?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I correct you? The closest military facility from the position where the shells fell is about 250 metres, and for an experienced artillery man, and given all the necessary atmospheric conditions, climatic, the qualitative choice of position for the artillery weapon, then the target will be hit within a range of 10 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the shelling was around midday, was it, in broad daylight, was it? Or was it at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was at 12.15, when the plateau was crowded, full of people, as we Bosniaks say, "God forbid". Had that shell fallen 20 metres further away, the minimum number of casualties would have been between 150 and 200, and among them the most numerous were elderly people and small children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you remember, what was the atmospheric conditions like and the visibility conditions at that time? Was it completely clear or was it completely obscure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can recollect, it was a fine spring sunny day, without any strong wind, which is one of the conditions required for the precision operation of artillery weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Witness W, we have now completed this long testimony. The Tribunal thanks you, both for the competent information which you have given to us and the availability which you showed both to the Prosecution which called you here and the Defence. The judges will now take approximately a 15 minute break, since we have already had one, and we are going to finish our work at about 5.45, therefore we will start again at around 5.00. Please do not move yet so that your protection can be ensured. (4.45 pm) (A short break) (5.10 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will now resume. Have the accused brought in, please. (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I am looking at the schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: My apologies, we forgot to offer into evidence the exhibits that we used. I had them all marked down. I think they were 81, 82 and 83 and they consist of the plastic foil that was put over the map, the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No objection on the part of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, looking at this week's schedule, if I am not wrong, we still have three witnesses to hear between now and 5.45 in order to complete your schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do believe, with all due respect, that several of those witnesses will be spending the weekend with us. I do not think it is feasible for us to get through three witnesses. We will carry them over until next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: For the most part, I think we can move through those witnesses relatively quickly, but I really do not see any other alternative at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Now we are going to have a witness who is not covered by protective measures, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, to the contrary. I believe at this point, and I have raised this with counsel, that this witness, because of his position, would mandate a closed session, in that because of his position, discussing the various matters that he will discuss, people will know who he is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Did you agree with the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We do not know who is next, your Honour. We have had various discussions about protected witnesses and I accept Mr. Kehoe's representation, but I am not sure exactly who the next witness is. I accept counsel's representation though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Maybe because this is Friday afternoon, but I suppose that is why you are in agreement in principle, even though we do not know which witness it is. I see the Defence is contributing to our discussions here. Very well, you are not going to give us the name of the witness, but we will go into closed session, but through the Registrar I would like to have the witness's name given to the Defence immediately, but do not state it until we have -- since we are going into closed session. (In closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
